bottom_line: Compared with placebo, apixaban 10 mg once daily increased major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (hazard ratio, 2.45; 95% confidence interval, 1.31 to 4.61; P⫽0.005).
implications: In this phase 2 ACS population, adding apixaban to antiplatelet therapy increased major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding versus placebo (e.g., 10 mg once daily HR 2.45; 95% CI 1.31 to 4.61; P⫽0.005; 2.5 mg twice daily HR 1.78; 95% CI 0.91 to 3.48; P⫽0.09). The composite ischemic outcome was numerically lower with apixaban vs placebo (2.5 mg twice daily HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.44 to 1.19; P⫽0.21; 10 mg once daily HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.35 to 1.04; P⫽0.07), but these estimates are not definitive given the confidence intervals and P values as reported.

major_points.text: Phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging trial in recent ACS patients on antiplatelet therapy.
major_points.quote:
APPRAISE was a phase 2,
  double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study.

major_points.text: Patients were randomized to placebo or one of four apixaban dosing regimens for 6 months.
major_points.quote:
Patients (n⫽1715) with recent ST-elevation or non–ST-elevation
  acute coronary syndrome were randomized to 6 months of placebo (n⫽611) or 1 of 4 doses of apixaban

major_points.text: Nearly all patients received aspirin and most received clopidogrel.
major_points.quote:
Nearly all patients
  received aspirin; 76% received clopidogrel.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.
major_points.quote:
The primary outcome was International Society of Thrombosis and
  Hemostasis major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.

major_points.text: Higher-dose apixaban arms were discontinued due to excess total bleeding.
major_points.quote:
At the recommendation of the Data Monitoring Committee, the
  2 higher-dose apixaban arms were discontinued because of excess total bleeding.

major_points.text: Apixaban increased major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding versus placebo in a dose-dependent manner for the two lower doses reported.
major_points.quote:
Compared with placebo, apixaban 2.5
  mg twice daily (hazard ratio, 1.78; 95% confidence interval, 0.91 to 3.48; P⫽0.09) and 10 mg once daily (hazard ratio,
  2.45; 95% confidence interval, 1.31 to 4.61; P⫽0.005)

major_points.text: Ischemic events were numerically lower with apixaban vs placebo for the two lower doses, with wide confidence intervals.
major_points.quote:
Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily (hazard ratio, 0.73; 95% confidence interval, 0.44 to 1.19;
  P⫽0.21) and 10 mg once daily (hazard ratio, 0.61; 95% confidence interval, 0.35 to 1.04; P⫽0.07)
